context: Feature concepts raised by Sean in the same session as the technical due-diligence follow-up. None of these exist in the codebase today (verified against Businessbear1981/Finesse-Life- as of this date) — this file captures them as build specs for Kevin/roadmap sequencing, separate from the existing bug-fix backlog (Scale join, Vault rate, agent query fixes, Market/Exchange wiring).

features.name: Real client interview + social/behavioral signal sourcing
features.one_liner: Replace the fake 'connected source' toggles with real OAuth-based ingestion so Style DNA is built from actual buying signals, not a boolean the LLM is told to believe.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. src/app/api/nightvision/analyze/route.ts takes sources.instagram/snapchat/plaid/spotify as plain booleans from the client — no OAuth flow, no token exchange, no real API calls to any of these platforms exist anywhere in the repo. The LLM is simply told 'Instagram is connected' as a string and fabricates plausible-sounding inferences.
depends_on: oauth app registration with each platform
token storage (social_accounts table already exists, unused for this)
consent/privacy copy update
build_spec: Real OAuth: Instagram Graph API (Basic Display or Graph API w/ Business login), Spotify Web API (Authorization Code flow), Plaid Link (transactions product) for real spend categories.
Store tokens encrypted in existing social_accounts table (access_token_enc column already there, unused).

Replace the boolean-flag prompt construction in analyze/route.ts with real fetched data: top Spotify artists/genres, Instagram media captions/hashtags (not photos, to start), Plaid merchant-category spend.
Self-learning loop: persist each analysis run + which signals fed it, so Style DNA visibly refines over time rather than being a single LLM call.
Flag for review, not a code fix: current system prompt hardcodes race/ethnicity-keyed brand and genre-to-brand recommendations. Needs a product/legal conversation before this ships to real users.
open_questions: Which platform first — Spotify is the lowest-friction OAuth (no app review needed for read-only scopes); Plaid requires a funded Plaid account and compliance review; Instagram Graph API requires Meta app review for anything beyond Basic Display.

features.name: Universal photo capture → auto-route to modules
features.one_liner: Snap a photo anywhere (in-app camera or upload) and have it automatically routed/tagged into Wardrobe (closet), Registry (wishlist), NIGHTVISION (style signal), and Embassy (deal matching) — one capture, many destinations.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. wardrobe_looks.photo_url and bag_items.photo_url exist as single-purpose upload fields (one photo, one destination, manual). Scout (src/lib/agents/scout.ts) has an image-analysis path but it's invoked per-search, not from a capture pipeline, and truncates the image to 200 chars — effectively non-functional today.
depends_on: Scout's image analysis actually working (currently broken — truncates base64 to 200 chars before sending to the LLM)
R2 upload flow
a routing/classification step to decide which module(s) a photo feeds
build_spec: Fix Scout's image path first — it can't classify anything today with a 200-char-truncated payload.

Single upload endpoint that: stores original to R2, runs one real vision-model call to classify (outfit item vs. wishlist item vs. general style signal), then fans out: wardrobe item -> bag_items/wardrobe_looks, wishlist-worthy -> wardrobe_wishlist/registry_items, always -> a NIGHTVISION style-signal event via the intelligence bus.
UI: a persistent capture affordance (camera button) available from Wardrobe, Registry, and the mobile shell, not a buried per-page upload form.
open_questions: Does this need a dedicated vision model call per photo (cost) or can it batch with existing Nova calls?

features.name: Nova-curated rotating outfit combinations
features.one_liner: Given a client's actual wardrobe items + occasion (business, nightwear, casual, event), Nova assembles and rotates complete outfit combinations (top/bottom/shoes/accessories) the client can browse and see 'what the intelligence picked.'
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Wardrobe today is a flat list/feed (wardrobe_looks, bag_items) with likes and a wishlist — no combination/outfit-building logic, no occasion tagging, no rotation.
depends_on: wardrobe items need structured attributes (category, formality, color, season) to combine algorithmically
Stylist agent (src/lib/agents/stylist.ts) already exists and is real (calls Claude) — natural place to extend
build_spec: Add occasion/formality/category tagging to bag_items (or a new wardrobe_items table if bag_items is meant to stay 'collection value' rather than 'wearable pieces').
Extend stylist.ts with an outfit-assembly mode: given occasion + wardrobe inventory, return N complete combinations, not just style advice text.
UI: a rotation/carousel view showing 'today's look' with a visible attribution ('Nova picked this because...') — matches the 'client can see what the intelligence picked' requirement.

Segmented carousel structure per Sean (2026-08-06): rotate by category zone, not just whole-outfit — waist-down (pants/shorts/skirts), tops/shirts, accessories, and dresses as their own full-torso rotation, rather than one single top-to-bottom carousel. Each zone should be independently swipeable so a client can hold a top constant and cycle bottoms against it, matching how people actually mix-and-match.
This is explicitly called out as equal priority to Per Diem (the men's date planner) — should get comparable design investment, not be an afterthought.
open_questions: Does this require the photo-capture pipeline to be live first (to populate real wardrobe inventory), or does it ship with manually-entered items?

features.name: Budget-constrained shopping companion — 'I want to shop for the gala but only have $X'
features.one_liner: A women's-side feature mirroring Per Diem's budget/planner pattern, but for shopping trips: set a hard budget for an event, get curated options that fit it.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT, but there is a close structural precedent to build from. src/app/(hotel)/perdiem/page.tsx (masculine side, date planner) already has a working budget-preset pattern (BUDGET_PRESETS: $100/$250/$500/$1000/no-limit) and a 'wishlist' tab with cheaper-alternative-brand suggestions (e.g. Loro Piana throw -> Jenni Kayne alternative at 1/3 the price) — same shape as what's being asked for, just needs to be event/shopping-framed instead of date-framed, and Per Diem itself is still demo-data-driven (DEMO_PLAN, DEMO_WISHLIST), not wired to real inventory.
depends_on: Scout/Price-Hunter agents (being fixed this session) for real product matching
a real catalog (flagged repo-wide as missing — currently seeds/hallucination per the June 23 audit)
build_spec: Reuse the Per Diem budget-preset UI pattern directly — don't redesign it, mirror it.
Occasion framing instead of date framing: 'gala,' 'wedding guest,' 'work event' as entry points instead of time-of-day date-plan slots.
Feed Scout/Price-Hunter with the occasion + budget ceiling; return options across price points that fit, with the same 'cheaper alternative' pattern Per Diem's wishlist already does.
Should NOT ship before Per Diem's own wishlist/planner is wired to real data — otherwise this inherits the same demo-data problem twice.

features.name: Ambassador program — passive income + agent outreach for opportunities
features.one_liner: Members can become ambassadors/affiliates earning passive income; an agent actively scouts ambassador/partnership opportunities through the client's own connected tech/social stack.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Embassy today (embassy_deals table) is staff-submitted partner deals only (status pending/review/live/rejected, submitted_by references a user) — there is no ambassador/affiliate-earnings concept, and no outreach agent of any kind.
depends_on: real social OAuth (same dependency as nightvision-real-signal-ingestion — can't scout 'opportunities through client's own stack' without real platform connections)
an affiliate/referral tracking layer (does not exist — Procurement's tokens are the closest analog and are fully mocked)
build_spec: This is a new agent role, not an extension of an existing one — closest existing pattern is procurement.ts's PARTNER_MAP, which would need to become a real affiliate-network integration (see research task on affiliate/ambassador platforms).
Needs a commission/earnings ledger — vault_transactions could carry this if extended, or a dedicated ambassador_earnings table.

Outreach agent scope is the least defined part of this — needs a product conversation on what 'looking for opportunities through the client's own stack' actually means operationally (is it: scanning their social posts for brand mentions to suggest affiliate links? Matching their follower count/niche to available partner programs? Something else?).
open_questions: What does 'agent outreach' mean concretely — outbound to brands on the member's behalf, or inbound matching to existing partner programs? This changes the build entirely.

features.name: On-demand agent swarm deployment for tasks/events
features.one_liner: Client can 'deploy' a swarm of agents against a specific task, bill, problem, interest, or event (a work gala, a birthday, a wedding) — purchased/triggered based on preference and timing rather than always-on.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. The intelligence engine (src/lib/intelligence/) and the 6 agents (stylist, scout, price-hunter, procurement, outing-planner, index) exist and are real, but they're invoked individually per-feature (e.g. Scout runs when you search), not as a coordinated, purchasable, event-triggered swarm.
depends_on: Stripe billing (Phase 1, already in progress per the roadmap) — 'purchase additional agents' implies a payment/entitlement model
an event/occasion trigger system (does not exist)
build_spec: Needs an orchestration layer above the individual agents — something that takes an occasion ('my sister's wedding, budget $2000, need outfit + gift + travel') and coordinates Stylist + Scout + Price-Hunter + Outing-Planner together against one goal, rather than the client invoking each separately.
Entitlement model: which agent combinations are free vs. paid add-ons needs product definition before engineering — this is a pricing/packaging decision, not just a build task.

Natural extension of the existing intelligence bus (src/lib/intelligence/bus.ts) — the emit() pattern already used by scale_join could generalize to 'event declared' -> 'swarm assembled' -> 'agents report back.'
open_questions: Is this priced per-swarm-deployment, a subscription tier unlock, or usage-based? Affects both the Stripe wiring in Phase 1 and the entitlement model above.

features.name: Match/rank Lounge members by taste similarity (style, music)
features.one_liner: Arrange or rank who a member sees in the Lounge by commonality of taste — shared music, style signals — rather than a flat chronological feed.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Lounge today (src/app/(hotel)/lounge/) is a flat social post feed — post-card.tsx, post-composer.tsx, page.tsx — reverse-chronological, no ranking or member-matching logic of any kind.
depends_on: nightvision-real-signal-ingestion — meaningful taste-similarity ranking needs real style/music signal, not the current fake boolean-flag system
a defined similarity metric (embedding distance on style_tags/brand_radar? shared Spotify genres, once real signal ingestion exists?)
build_spec: Short term (works today without waiting on real OAuth): rank by overlap of existing NIGHTVISION style_tags/brand_radar and the intake 'vibe' field — weak signal, but real and already-stored, unlike fabricated social data.
Long term: once real Spotify/Instagram signal exists (see nightvision-real-signal-ingestion), compute similarity from actual genre/artist overlap and style embeddings.
Needs a product decision: is this a visible 'ranked by compatibility' UI, or an invisible feed-ordering signal? Very different UX and privacy implications.
open_questions: Does surfacing 'you're similar to this person' explicitly raise different privacy/consent expectations than silently reordering a feed?

features.name: Light post-interaction feedback to refine profiling
features.one_liner: After a Nova-planned date/outing, capture lightweight, non-judgmental feedback that feeds back into the user's profile — not a rating of the other person, but insight into the user's own interests, values, and what mattered to them.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. planOuting (src/lib/agents/outing-planner.ts) produces a plan; nothing captures what happened afterward or feeds it back into behavioral profiling. The intelligence bus (src/lib/intelligence/bus.ts, emit()) already supports arbitrary signal events, so the plumbing to receive this exists — there's just no capture point or UI for it yet.
depends_on: outing-planner's plan needs a stable reference ID to attach post-outing feedback to (check whether one already exists)
build_spec: Explicitly framed as insight-gathering, not a partner rating system — e.g. 'what mattered most about tonight?' with open/tag-based responses (values, interests), not a 1-5 star judgment of the other person.
Feed responses into buildBehavioralProfile (src/lib/intelligence/behavioral.ts) as a new signal type alongside existing category/brand affinities.
Timing/UX matters a lot here — needs to feel like a warm check-in from Nova, not a survey, or it won't get used.
open_questions: Where does this prompt surface — push notification next-day, in-app on next Nova session, both?

features.name: Standing agent workforce: per-room agents, deal-sourcing agents, client-signal monitors, internal ops agents
features.one_liner: Move from 'agents you call per-request' to a standing multi-agent architecture: each room has a dedicated agent optimizing its own products/content, Scale has deal-sourcing agents working different tiers, a monitoring layer continuously watches member preference/traffic/buying signals, and a separate internal agent stack watches platform health — all self-learning, API-driven, fed by real social wiring and NIGHTVISION.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT — and structurally different from what exists, not just missing pieces of it. Today: exactly one dispatch endpoint (src/app/api/agents/route.ts) with 5 stateless agents (scout, stylist, procurement, price-hunter, outing-planner) that only execute when a request calls them. No agent 'owns' a room. No continuous/background monitoring process exists — the closest thing is the intelligence bus (src/lib/intelligence/bus.ts, emit()) which is a passive event log, not an active monitoring agent. No agent operates on the platform's own internal health/user base as a subject.
depends_on: nightvision-real-signal-ingestion — 'client signal monitoring' needs real signal to monitor, not the current fake booleans
a background job/scheduling layer — nothing in this Next.js app runs on a timer or continuously today; everything is request-triggered

intelligence-agent-swarm-deployment (already in this file) — related but distinct: that entry is member-triggered/event-triggered swarms for a specific occasion; this is standing, always-on agent ownership
build_spec: Per-room agents: define what 'optimizing a room' concretely means per room before building anything — e.g. for Scale, an agent might mean 'surface the highest-conversion-probability deals to the top'; for Wardrobe, 'suggest what to retire/add.' This needs a per-room product spec, not one generic template.

Scale-tier deal-sourcing agents: this is the operational side of the affiliate-network research already done (Impact.com etc.) — an agent role that actively works partner-network APIs looking for new deals/partnerships to bring in, not just executing a search when a member asks.

Client-signal monitoring layer: extend behavioral.ts (src/lib/intelligence/behavioral.ts) from 'compute a profile when asked' to 'continuously update and flag notable pattern changes' — needs a scheduled job runner (Vercel Cron, or a queue), which doesn't exist in this codebase yet.
Internal ops agent stack: needs explicit scoping — is this fraud/abuse detection, engagement/churn-risk monitoring, infra health, or all three? Each is a different build.

Self-learning loop: every agent above should feed back into NIGHTVISION/behavioral profiles rather than being a one-off output — the intelligence bus is the right existing primitive to extend, not replace.
open_questions: This is a significant infrastructure investment (background job runner, per-room product specs, monitoring/alerting) — does it belong before or after the Phase 1 transact sprint? Recommend after: none of this generates revenue on its own, and it's easier to build agent ownership on top of a product that already has real payment/commerce wiring than to build it on top of mocks.

Sequencing suggestion: real signal ingestion (nightvision-real-signal-ingestion) and a background job runner are the two prerequisites everything else in this entry depends on — those two would be the actual first build steps, not the per-room agents themselves.

features.name: Spades + Poker pilot, active-member-only, small scale
features.one_liner: Spades and Poker via an existing third-party gaming platform, scoped specifically to Carpe Diem (masculine edition), gated to 'active member' status rather than full VIP, and deliberately small-scale/pilot-framed to work out bugs before any wider rollout.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. 'Game Room' already appears as a nav link in the live site's room rail (confirmed via direct fetch of finesselife.vip) alongside Lounge/Entourage/Lab/Switchboard/Lair/Vault/Scale/Nova/Exchange/Embassy — but there is no corresponding page anywhere in src/app/ for it. It's a nav entry with nothing behind it, same class of issue as other mock surfaces found this session.
depends_on: Confirm what 'active member' means precisely as a gate — likely profiles.status = 'active' (set post-onboarding per the SOP), which is broader than VIP/subscription_tier. Needs a decision: is this its own narrower cohort flag, or literally just 'onboarding complete'?
identifying a real third-party gaming platform with an embeddable/API integration path for Spades and Poker with private-room support — not yet researched this session
build_spec: Explicit build direction from Sean: use an existing gaming platform (not custom-built game logic) for both Spades and Poker.

Explicitly scoped as a small-scale pilot on Carpe Diem only, gated to active-member status — not a full VIP/Backstage launch. Framing is 'work out the bugs' before considering wider rollout (Per Diem side, broader membership tiers).
Private room setup is a named requirement — members should be able to create a table for their own group, not just join a public table.

Poker specifically may carry real-money-gaming regulatory exposure depending on whether stakes are involved — flag for a legal read if any wagering (even Vault-credit-based) is considered, separate from a pure-social/no-stakes version.
open_questions: Is this social/no-stakes play, or could members wager Vault credits? The second option reopens gambling-regulation questions similar in spirit to the Vault money-transmitter flag already in the roadmap.
Which third-party platform — needs its own research pass before a build spec can be concrete.
features.risk_flag: Sean suggested Bovada specifically as the third-party platform. FLAGGING, NOT ADOPTING: Bovada is an offshore sportsbook/casino operating without a license in most/all US states — it has been the subject of state Attorney General cease-and-desist actions (Washington State, among others). Integrating or linking a legitimate, investor-facing platform to an unlicensed offshore gambling operator is a real legal and reputational exposure, comparable in severity to the Vault money-transmitter question already in the roadmap but without an obvious compliant path the way Stripe Issuing provides for Vault. Piloting small and active-member-only reduces exposure surface but does not remove the underlying legal question — recommend resolving the platform choice before any integration work, not after.

features.name: Barcode/SKU scanning for verified designer, size, and fit data
features.one_liner: Add a barcode/product-tag scanner (alongside the plain photo capture just built) so items are identified with real SKU-level data — designer, size, fit, material — instead of inferred purely from a photo.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. The photo-capture pipeline built 2026-08-06 (PhotoCaptureGrid in nightvision/page.tsx) sends raw photos to Nova for visual inference only — no barcode/UPC decoding, no SKU lookup against any product database.
depends_on: a barcode-decoding library on the client (e.g. a JS barcode/QR scanner using the device camera) — nothing like this exists in the repo today
a product/SKU lookup source once a barcode is decoded — UPC databases exist (e.g. UPCitemdb, Barcode Lookup API) but have not been researched or selected this session
wardrobe-photo-capture-pipeline (already in this file) — barcode scanning is a precision upgrade to that pipeline, not a separate capture flow
build_spec: Add a scan mode to PhotoCaptureGrid (or a new capture surface) using a client-side barcode decoder against the device camera.

On successful decode, look up the UPC/EAN against a product database API to pull verified brand/designer, category, and (where available) size/fit metadata — falls back to Nova's visual inference when no barcode is present or the lookup misses.

Store decoded SKU data alongside the existing photo record (bag_items/wardrobe_looks or a new table) so downstream signal (style-quality scoring, Scale opportunity detection) can use structured designer/size data instead of just LLM-inferred labels.
This is the foundation the other two new entries below (style-quality signal, Scale opportunity detection) get meaningfully more accurate with — recommend sequencing this before those, not after.
open_questions: Which UPC lookup provider — cost and coverage vary a lot; needs a research pass before implementation, same as the affiliate-network research already done for Embassy.

features.name: Self-learning style-quality signal with gamified, subtle hinting
features.one_liner: Beyond just building a Style DNA description, have the system form a quiet, self-improving judgment of how strong a member's actual style/wardrobe is, and surface that as gentle, non-insulting hints and gamified prompts ('your fit could use range in outerwear') rather than a blunt score.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Today NIGHTVISION only produces a descriptive style_dna/brand_radar/style_tags summary (src/app/api/nightvision/analyze/route.ts) — it is affirming-by-design (the system prompt explicitly says 'be direct and confident, no hedging') and has no notion of quality, gaps, or improvement suggestions at all.
depends_on: wardrobe-photo-capture-pipeline and nightvision-barcode-sku-identification (both in this file) — meaningful quality signal needs a real wardrobe inventory (verified pieces, not just a handful of onboarding photos) to judge gaps/range/quality against
a defined rubric for what 'good style' means well enough to hint at without being reductive or offensive — this is a product/editorial decision, not purely an engineering one
build_spec: Extend behavioral.ts / the NIGHTVISION profile with a private 'style range' signal computed from actual wardrobe inventory (category coverage, price-tier consistency, versus what similar high-affinity members hold) — never shown as a raw score to the member.

Surface findings only as soft, actionable hints inside Nova conversation or a wardrobe UI nudge (e.g. 'You're strong in eveningwear — light on tailored daywear') — framed as an opportunity, never a deficiency callout. This needs real copywriting/editorial review before shipping, not just an engineering pass.

Gamification layer: badges/progress toward 'range' completeness, tied to actual capture activity (uploading more photos/scans increases signal fidelity) — gives members a reason to keep feeding the system, which also compounds the self-learning loop.

Self-learning loop: every wardrobe addition should re-run the range/gap computation, same durable-cache pattern already used for buildBehavioralProfile (src/lib/intelligence/profile-store.ts, 15-min freshness) rather than recomputing from scratch each time.
open_questions: Who defines the 'good style' rubric this scores against — an internal stylist/editorial team, or purely peer-comparison against other members' verified wardrobes (which sidesteps taste judgments but needs enough member data to be meaningful)?

features.name: Aggregate wardrobe/barcode signal feeds Scale deal-sourcing and a potential Finesse-branded product line
features.one_liner: As members capture real wardrobe photos and barcodes, aggregate the signal across the member base to (1) actively hunt matching deals/discounts for items members already want, (2) detect trending items early enough to launch a real-time Scale group-buy or Embassy deal, and eventually (3) justify a private-label Finesse product (e.g. a manufacturer run of a popular scarf/jacket silhouette) once demand signal is strong enough. Sean explicitly talked through and set aside a broader 'thrift-store-style peer marketplace' framing as out of scope for now — 'that's too much, our own brand and scale is a good idea' — so this entry is scoped to demand-signal-driven sourcing/private-label, not a peer-to-peer resale marketplace.
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Scale (scale_deals/scale_joins) and Embassy (embassy_deals) are both currently either staff-seeded or staff-submitted — no aggregate member-demand signal feeds either today, and there is no private-label/manufacturing pathway anywhere in the codebase or docs.
depends_on: nightvision-barcode-sku-identification (this file) — trend/demand detection is far more reliable off verified SKU data than off photo-only inference
wardrobe-photo-capture-pipeline (this file) — needs volume of real capture activity across the member base before any aggregate signal is meaningful

intelligence-agent-swarm-deployment / multi-agent-operations-architecture (this file) — this is exactly the kind of standing, always-on deal-sourcing agent role already scoped generally in multi-agent-operations-architecture; this entry is the concrete Scale/Embassy application of that idea

a real manufacturing/sourcing relationship before the private-label piece is anything but a roadmap idea — no vendor research has been done this session (distinct from the existing Alibaba/Amazon-MCF unit-economics note in CONTEXT.md for the Scale model generally)
build_spec: Phase 1 (deal-hunting agent): extend the existing agent pattern (src/lib/agents/) with a standing role that takes aggregate wardrobe/wishlist signal (categories, brands, price tiers members are capturing) and actively searches for matching discounts/deals to feed into Scale or Embassy — this is the operational Scale/Embassy application of the deal-sourcing agent role already scoped in multi-agent-operations-architecture.

Phase 2 (trend detection): once barcode/SKU data gives verified designer+item identity, detect repeated captures of the same or highly similar SKU across multiple members within a time window — that's the 'signal to launch a real-time Scale/Embassy deal on the thing that's suddenly hot' capability.

Phase 3 (private label, speculative/long-horizon): if trend detection repeatedly surfaces strong demand for a specific silhouette/category, that becomes a data-backed case for a Finesse-branded manufacturing run — explicitly the long-horizon payoff Sean described, not a near-term build. Needs real sourcing/manufacturing partnership work before this is anything but a roadmap flag.

Explicitly NOT in scope per Sean's own scoping-down in this conversation: a peer-to-peer 'thrift store' resale marketplace where members sell directly to each other — Exchange (src/app/api/exchange/) already covers peer resale in a narrower form; this entry is about demand-signal-driven sourcing and private label, not expanding peer resale.
open_questions: What volume of member capture activity is needed before aggregate signal is statistically meaningful rather than noise? Needs a data/product decision once nightvision-barcode-sku-identification and the photo-capture pipeline are actually live and generating real volume.

Manufacturing/private-label is a genuinely separate business line (sourcing, MOQs, inventory risk) from the software platform — worth a dedicated business-planning conversation, not something to scope as an engineering task alongside the rest of this file.

features.name: AI-generated 3D model of the client's actual body for pre-purchase fit preview
features.one_liner: Generate a 3D model sized to the client's real body (not a generic mannequin) and render prospective clothing on it, so a member can see how a piece will actually fit before buying — Sean's framing: 'never go to the store and find out these jeans won't fit.'
features.current_state: NOT BUILT. Nothing in the repo does body measurement capture, 3D avatar generation, or garment-fit simulation of any kind. media_jobs/media_assets (R2-backed) handle flat image/video generation only — no 3D asset pipeline exists.
depends_on: a body-measurement capture method — options range from a short guided-photo capture (2-4 photos, similar to how e.g. 3DLOOK/Presize-style products work) to manual measurement entry; full accuracy needs the former, which is a real computer-vision problem, not a prompt-engineering one

a garment-fit rendering pipeline — this is the hard, genuinely novel part: draping/simulating a specific garment's actual cut and size chart onto a body-accurate 3D mesh is a distinct technical discipline from image generation, and no existing Finesse infrastructure does this

a real product/garment catalog with actual size charts and, ideally, garment mesh/pattern data per SKU — connects directly to the missing-real-catalog gap already flagged in the June 23 due-diligence audit, and to nightvision-barcode-sku-identification (this file) for verified item identity
build_spec: This is not a small feature — treat as its own project with a build-vs-buy decision up front. Existing virtual-try-on/body-fit vendors (Zeekit — acquired by Walmart and not available as a third-party API since; 3DLOOK; Presize; Vue.ai) exist and solve pieces of this; a build-vs-license research pass should happen before any custom engineering starts.
Phase 1 (measurement capture): guided photo or manual-measurement intake added to the intake/NIGHTVISION flow, stored on the member profile.

Phase 2 (avatar generation): generate a body-accurate 3D mesh/avatar from captured measurements — likely a licensed third-party model rather than something built in-house, given the specialized computer-vision expertise required.

Phase 3 (garment fit rendering): drape/render a specific SKU (from a real catalog with size-chart or pattern data) onto the avatar — the hardest and most novel piece; realistically needs either a specialized vendor or a dedicated ML effort, not a quick integration.

Sean's 'perhaps issue a free fitting to all clients' idea — a complimentary/included virtual-fitting session as a membership perk — is a packaging/pricing decision to revisit once Phases 1-3 have a real technical path, not before.
open_questions: Build vs. license — given the specialized 3D/computer-vision work involved, licensing an existing virtual-try-on vendor is very likely faster and cheaper than building this in-house; needs a vendor research pass (comparable to the affiliate-network and UPC-lookup research already flagged elsewhere in this file) before committing either way.

This has a hard dependency on a real product catalog with actual size/fit data per SKU — without that, there is nothing to fit the avatar against no matter how good the avatar generation is. Sequencing-wise this likely sits well behind nightvision-barcode-sku-identification and the general 'no real catalog exists' gap from the June 23 audit.
